chunks: From him, from Ibrahim, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"You have the option to return the gift as long as it remains in your possession; but when it goes out to its owner, you do not have the right to take it back."
And he said, "The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever returns his gift is like the one who returns his vomit.'"

key_terms.الْخِيَار: Option or right of choice (here, right of revocation)

ai.seo_question: Can a donor take back a gift after giving it?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the revocability of gifts (*hibah*) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between the donor's right to retract while the item remains in their possession and the finality of transfer to the recipient. The Prophetic analogy of 'returning one's vomit' (*al-raj' ila qay'ihi*) underscores the naturalness of revocation before transfer but the awkwardness and finality once completed, a principle widely cited by scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Tusi to define the conditions of *hibah* validity.
